spoilers extended back to the dance part 11 strategy in the dance 130131 ac thanks once again to everyone thats followed this series so far part 10 is here in case you missed previous installments this one went long again so ill link the full analysis here and try to put as much of it down below as i can as for why it took me so long to get through part 11 well i took a break after part 10 to avoid getting burned out and imay have written 80 of an entirely new series that will act as a sequel to this one oops once i finish the conclusion to this series ill start on the new one which covers targaryenseven kingdoms history from 136 ac to 196 ac so from the end of aegon iiis regency to the end of the first blackfyre rebellion if that scratches an itch for you then stay tuned welcome back to our secondtolast installment of this analysis and the conclusion to our discussion of strategy in the dance our focus is the period after second tumbleton to aegon iiis coronation in 131 ac although strictly speaking the only events were concerned with are those of 131 both factions leave much to be desired in terms of their use of strategy as weve seen from part eight onwards and the final campaigns of 131 continue this trend when it comes to the end of the dance as it plays out in the hour of the wolf my approach will be more akin to our analyses in parts nine and ten i believe there is more going on in fbs account than meets the eye and this is clear when we closely scrutinize gyldans account and those of his sources without further ado lets begin i going nowhere fast everyone edition well start by establishing as accurate a timeline as possible before analyzing the events of 131 after rhaenyras death on october 22nd 130 ac aegon ii and his allies remain on dragonstone as of december 9th when sunfyre dies of his wounds aegon had returned to kings landing by december 31st punishing the various factions that held sway in the moon of the three kings skipping ahead aegon iii and jaehaeras wedding and coronation were held on july 7th 131 sometime after the hour of the wolf with the high septon travelling from oldtown to officiate i noted in part 13 the original analysis that atlas of ice and fires distance map estimates the travel time from oldtown to kings landing at roughly 40 days and two months seems like a reasonable estimate in this instance due to the winter weather the dangers of road travel and the fellow travelers joining the high septon this would put the end of the hour at roughly may 7th while twoiaf gives a week for the hour itself with the false dawn that preceded the hour covering the better part of a fortnight and the muddy mess before it taking place two days march from kings landing this means that aegon ii ruled for four months at most between his return to the capital in midtolate december and the date of the muddy mess around april 15th this is important for the analysis which follows as events take place very quickly within a short amount of time and this affects how we assess the policies and strategy of both sides the most obvious challenge for assessing strategy is the lack of a central leadership for the blacks if we look at history king stephens supporters still had his wife queen matilda and their children to look to when the king was captured at lincoln the yorkists still had edward iv and his brothers after duke richard was killed at wakefield in 1460 and the lancastrians could still look to queen margaret and prince edward even while henry vi was held captive by the yorkists at various points prior to the readeption in 147071 by contrast rhaenyra and daemon are dead their only known living son is a hostage of aegon ii along with one of daemons daughters and rhaenyras former greatest ally corlys velaryon has turned coat to support the greens dalton greyjoy is the only supporter of rhaenyra still engaged in any fighting purely for his own gain the vale has played no part in the dance and neither has the north outside the winterwolves and the white harbour contingent in kings landing while the riverlands has suffered from aemonds attacks and the campaigns of the previous two years and is now led by elmo tully a neutral lord aside from his intervention at second tumbleton by comparison the greens once more have their king who also has an heir in his daughter jaehaera and could potentially father more by his betrothal to cassandra baratheon he controls the capital once more and still controls the dispersed royal treasury while corlys velaryons allegiance gives him the velaryon fleet the stormlords are now firmly on his side and he can potentially raise more forces from the westerlands and reach and his previous supporters in the riverlands and crownlands cannot be discounted either with winter now being almost a year old by the start of 131 it might be expected that the greens would be the favoured faction in any further hostilities this ends up not being the case but twoiaf and fb offer similar but ultimately contradictory explanations as to why the former states that though rhaenyra was dead and aegon the younger was in his hands aegon ii still had enemies who continued to fight against him albeit they fought as much out of fear of his reprisals as they did for rhaenyra in other words the blacks elected to fight on regardless of their lack of a viable claimant to the throne but while fear of reprisals also comes up in fb in the case of the riverlords elmo tully cregan stark and jeyne arryn are portrayed not as continuing an existing struggle with existing troops but mobilizing entirely in response to aegon iis campaign against the crownlands lords sometime after his rule is reestablished in kings landing aegon ii sends his own troops with borros baratheon and his stormlanders to subdue rosby stokeworth and duskendale arresting their lords and forcing their houses to pay ransoms and give hostages in return for their release although this seems to ignore that the lords of rosby and stokeworth are children and lady darklyn rules duskendale according to gyldan king aegon ii might reasonably have expected the remaining opposition to his rule to melt away but rather than heed corlys velaryon and issue a general pardon for the lords and ladies that supported rhaenyra the campaign against the crownlanders proved a grave mistake for it only served to harden the hearts of the late queens men against the king reports are soon received of northern troops gathering at winterfell barrowtown and white harbour jeyne arryn assembles 1500 knights and 8000 men at arms which is subsequently upgraded to 10000 men altogether in addition to sending envoys to braavos to arrange ships for transport and elmo tully raises close to 6000 men with support from the blackwoods freys mallisters darrys brackens and vances of wayfarers rest the issue with this is that aside from the riverlords the other black forces must travel great distances under less than ideal circumstances to even reach kings landing to which we can add the time required to actually raise their troops in response to aegon iis campaign assuming aegon ii returned to the capital by the end of 130 ac if we allow two weeks for his forces to plan and execute the crownlands campaign and another two weeks for news of it to reach the blacks this only leaves twoandahalf months until the muddy mess and three months until the hour of the wolf the valemen arrive at maidenpool and duskendale shortly after the muddy mess which further reduces the amount of time available for rhaenyras allies to formulate plans mobilize their forces and reach the points expected of them by the plot in part two we estimated that the distance between lord harroways town and kings landing is less than 400 miles as the crow flies and less than 200 miles between lord harroways town and riverrun or at least 50 days marching at 12 miles per day elmo tully would have just under a month at least to formulate his plans and mobilize his forces which is not unthinkable given how close many of his supporters are to riverrun such as the brackens and blackwoods while the darrys are far to the east and could join them on the march the same cannot be said for the northerners or the valemen as the time allotted is nowhere near enough for either force atlas distance map estimates the travel time from winterfell to kings landing at 40 days but this is based on distance as the crow flies and traveling on horseback at 25 miles per day with minimal baggage and access to remounts cregan starks host travelled on foot so far as we can tell and numbered between 8 and 10000 men with the former being munkuns estimate and supported by elio garcia and the latter the figure promised by cregan in his reply to rhaenyras letters at duskendale at 12 miles per day or roughly twice as long as atlas estimate it would take 80 days or almost three months for cregans forces to reach kings landing this would line up with our estimates but only if cregans forces set out immediately at the end of january allowing no time for mobilization or any other delays it should be noted that george seems to have a much different frame of reference for marching times in fb as we noted in part nine that the distance from kings landing to harrenhal would be just under 400 miles at least and aemond and coles forces made the journey in 20 days or four days longer than expected they did so in inclement weather with a mostly footbound army and a large baggage train managing under 20 miles a day at least which is considered slow going by the story despite exceeding 12 miles per day by a few miles at least even so the northern army must mobilize across much greater distances and travel during winter in 132 ac a year or so after the dance ends were told it took benjicot blackwood and his retinue thrice as long as expected to reach winterfell for cregan stark and alysanne blackwoods wedding due to the winter conditions the vales situation isnt much better as the passes through the mountains of the moon have been closed by the winter weather and the vale must rely on braavosi ships since the story decides that they lack their own leaving aside the fact that the largest viable ports on the eastern coastmaidenpool duskendale and kings landingare at least nominally greenheld obtaining ships also presents a problem sellsails would be needed to oppose the velaryon fleet in addition to the ships necessary to transport 10000 men plus supplies and horses which begs the question as to how jeyne arryn has the funds to hire such a force and why this played no role in rhaenyras war effort actually getting them to gulltown is another story as gyldans account of alyn velaryons campaigns in the stepstones and against dalton greyjoy provides us with information about winter sailing in the setting strong north winds prevail upon the narrow sea which allows alyns forces to make excellent time in reaching the stepstones while alyn must later beat eastward ie sail into the wind to cross the southern coast of dorne on his return to kings landing this suggests that the prevailing winds on planetos function much like they do on earth being northerly and westerly in the winter as they form in the north and travel south and west with gulltown being far to the south and west of braavos this means that the ships jeyne arryn hired would be able to reach gulltown in good time but those of her envoys sailing to braavos to hire said ships would be against the wind the entire journey adding to their travel time and delaying the embarkation of the vale forces fbs account of the beginnings of the final campaigns of the dance is effectively unworkable as it requires the blacks to do too much in too little time twoiafs account is much simpler and more feasible though it would alter the conclusions of fb by having the blacks already intent on removing aegon ii and would make the crownlands campaign merely an excuse to act the disunity of the blacks creates another problem for the story namely that the greens are completely ignorant of this and do nothing to exploit it diplomatically the only real excuse that can be offered is that the likes of corlys velaryon and larys strong had no intention of delivering victory for aegon ii and sabotaged his war effort but even this doesnt account for the ignorance of the rest of the green council elmo tully was neutral prior to second tumbleton and his stated aims appear defensive in nature jeyne arryn has loose family ties to rhaenyra and aegon iii and currently has princess rhaena as her guest but the vale has played no part in the dance thus far and cregan stark is an unknown quantity to both sides since the only aid he provided to rhaenyra was the winter wolves not one of these three tripped over themselves to aid rhaenyra after her flight from kings landing certainly not elmo tully based on our analysis of his motivations in part ten not only does their disunity create problems for coordinating their armies it presents opportunities for aegon ii and his council to negotiate separately with them and weaken the blacks before they even march the passes in the mountains of the moon have been snowedin as of maiden day 130 ac while threatening the vale by sea requires attacking the fortified and defended port of gulltown the north is even more inaccessible due to weather and distance so aegon ii cannot pose an immediate threat to the vale or the north leaving the riverlords as the only party facing any sort of risk unfortunately fb presents continued warfare and reprisals or the blanket pardons advocated by corlys velaryon as the only options available to the greens even though this is by no means the case ii strategy im more of a battleship guy myself the problems with the beginnings of the final campaign are compounded by the complete absence of strategy from either sides actions i noted in part nine that the westerlands role in aemonds strategy ignores the better options utilized by jaime and tywin lannister in agot during their invasion of the riverlands and this is once more the case with the greens in 131 ac only tywin is the one being ignored rather than jaime while jaime scatters edmure tullys forces and lays siege to riverrun thus tying down the strength of the riverlords tywin follows the gold road to the kingsroad and marches north occupying the inn at the crossroads and the surrounding territories this prevented robb stark and his army from joining forces with his mothers bannermen to the south or his aunt lysas bannermen to the southeast as tywin could confront robbs forces heading south and headoff any vale army marching down the high road of course the vale remains neutral and robb is able to overcome the strategic bind tywin places him in but the main point is that tywins actions show how an effective strategy can neutralize multiple opponents by securing key communications points to constrain their freedom to act this is relevant for the greens position in 131 ac since they are faced with multiple opponents from the same kingdomsthe riverlands north and valeand should be able to formulate similar plans to confront them duskendale and kings landing are held by the greens in the latter case and can be protected by the velaryon fleet in both instances leaving maidenpool the only port that could potentially disembark jeyne arryns 10000 men manfryd mooton raised aegons standard after the nettles affair at least according to their own chronicles but even if they were only nominally loyal to aegon in 131 occupying or besieging maidenpool with his army would allow aegon ii to deny the vale forces a proper landing site for their men horses supplies and equipment this would already neutralize one army and maidenpools location east of the kingsroad while not directly obstructing the advance of the riverlords or the northerners would force both hosts to go out of their way to confront the green army or risk their columns being attacked from the rear and flank as they tried to advance south it would also offer a base for mounted troops to carry out scorched earth tactics against the areas astride the kingsroad and harass the advancing columns impeding their movement and further requiring them to confront aegon iis army instead the greens all but twiddle their thumbs waiting on reinforcements from farafield and only sally forth against the blacks when the riverlords are two days march from kings landing but even the blacks are poorly served by the narrative just as tywins strategic moves placed robb stark in a difficult position at the twins prior to the battle of the green fork robb was able to escape this predicament through an alliance with the freys leading his mounted troops south to riverrun and gathering riverlord support before surprising jaime at riverrun while tywin was deceived into committing all his strength against roose bolton and the northern foot likewise the blacks also have solutions to the strategic bottleneck the greens could create by securing maidenpool solutions which are seemingly unnecessary only because the story makes the greens entirely passive in the face of their enemies the riverlords and northerners allow themselves to be bottlenecked by relying upon the kingsroad but this can be avoided by using different routes which force the greens to contend with attacks from multiple axes based on the arryn forces landings at duskendale and maidenpool they would most likely make use of the rosby and duskendale roads to reach kings landing while cregans forces are marching south via the kingsroad the riverlords also utilized the kingsroad but there is another option that would allow them to confront aegon ii in birth death and betrayal under king jaehaerys i on pg 206 of fb gyldan tells us that jaehaerys 5253 ac new year progress in the riverlands travelled from riverrun to stoney sept via acorn hall pinkmaiden and atranta while jaehaerys retinues on his progresses were not large this was also nearly a decade before jaehaerys began the royal roads project so the disadvantages of a local road like this compared to the major roads would not have been as great as in later decades if jason lannisters 8000 strong host was able to use local roads to reach the gods eye in 130 ac with lord lefford being their only impediment i see no reason why the riverlords could not march south to stoney sept and follow the gold road and the blackwater rush to kings landing from the west this would allow them to use the red fork and the rush to assist with transporting supplies and even troops while attacking from the west forces aegon ii to contend with multiple armies on multiple fronts holding maidenpool would still create problems for the valemen and the northerners but it would also allow the riverlords to cut off aegon iis army from kings landing by approaching the city far to their rear even if aegon confronts the riverlords first this still buys time for the northerners to continue south and for the vale ships to approach maidenpool iii truly one of the battles of time all of this lacklustre strategy and setup culminates in the final battle of the dance the battle of the kingsroad or the muddy mess as it is better known fought two days march from kings landing it was nigh unto dusk according to gyldan when the battle began with the stormlords attacking the riverlord host in its position on the kingsroad between a low hill and a wood emboldened by his scouts reports that the riverlords were led by women and boys borros baratheon led the attack up the road at the head of his cavalry in wedge formation with his foot following behind and the crownlanders held in reserve owing to rainfall over the past few days which left the ground soggy and alysanne blackwoods archers targeting them from the low hill less than half of the cavalry reached the riverlords shield wall while the rest had their horses shot from beneath them but the arrival of the stormlord foot threatened to breakthrough benjicot blackwood attacked from the woods on the left shattering the stormlord ranks while the hayford stokeworth and rosby men dipped their banners when borros sounded the horn for reinforcements the duskendale knights attacked the stormlanders while the kings landing levies broke and fled although borros succeeded in cutting down lords mallister and darry before kermit tully cut him down and ended the battle i covered the muddy mess in part 12 of the original series but it warrants greater attention owing to our coverage of ground warfare in part three of this series the failures of either side to effectively strategize compound the problems with the battle itself as the greens allow the riverlords to come within a six day march of kings landing before taking any action despite fb depicting aegon ii as unwilling to consider peace while borros baratheon holds his opponents in contempt hayford is a days march north of kings landing according to jaime iii of affc while rosby stokeworth and duskendale are not in the immediate path of the riverlord advance with or without a march to maidenpool as we proposed borros has no reason not try and head off the riverlords with his own forces at a location of his choosing along the kingsroad no attempt is made to employ the stormlands and crownlands mounted troops to harass the riverlords or deny them resources through scorched earth even though someone like borros baratheon with experience fighting the dornish should have some familiarity with these tactics while the battle itself begins when he chooses to attack the riverlords in their own defensive position this latter point is especially problematic when we consider the conspicuous absence of longbowmen from borros army twoiaf praises the longbowmen of the dornish marches as perhaps the finest in westeros something which i also discussed in part 5 of the dorne series as we noted in part three longbows were an important part of defensive tactics since their range and rate of fire allowed them to engage a foe in a defensive position at a distance goading them into attacking in order to remove the threat of ones archery and thereby forcing the enemy to attack into your own prepared defenses confronting the riverlords from his own defensive position is an option denied to borros by the plot as is the option of showering his opponent with arrows in order to force an advance but whereas the westerlands host at the lakeshore had archers and did not appear to use them we have no indications of the make up of borros host beyond the infantry and cavalry split so far are we know he may have no archers at all how convenient leaving aside the archers the logic of the attack still makes no sense as its justified by women and youths being the leaders of the riverlord host we know that lords mallister darry bracken and vance were part of the host albeit hugo vance was young and gyldan later tells us there were other lords and famous knights among the ranks of the host if borros holds the likes of alysanne and benjicot blackwood sabitha frey and the tully brothers in low regard why should he even assume that his scouts were correct and conclude that the older men were in charge and thus tailor his plans accordingly there was clearly an outcome in mind for this plot but there is nothing believable about how the plot reaches that outcome to begin with as the rest of the battle makes abundantly clear the first action of the battle the stormlords cavalry charge has a plethora of issues beginning with the circumstances of said charge borros has 600 knights under his command and this is a suitable force for making a charge based on the numbers we discussed in part three but we unfortunately cant be sure of the frontage of the two armies or any distances on the battlefield the frontage seems sufficient for borros infantry to come to grips with the riverlords across their entire line while leaving an open flank for benjicot to exploit while at the same time the riverlords kept deep enough ranks to replace the ranks of those who fell against borros knights large though the wedge might be it would still probably risk being enveloped attacking the center of the line unless the charge was delivered with sufficient speed and cohesion to effect a roulement perptuel ie breaking through the enemy lines and reforming to attack again from the rear the muddy ground and wet grass would obviously present problems even without black aly and her archers while the earlier arrival of dusk which we could expect thanks to it being winter would make coordinating the advance that much more difficult on the other hand the fact that alysannes archers would be on the far right of the line combined with the low light conditions owing to the sun setting behind their low hill makes it questionable that the archers could shoot down the horses beneath borros riders as gyldan describes when their position would allow them to drop their arrows into the wedge and its exposed flank the unhorsing of more than half of the stormlands knights implies that their horses were unbarded a serious problem we discussed in part three which makes it unlikely that the disordered ranks that reached the shield wall would be able to engage in any sort of melee despite gyldans claim that borros men wreaked great havoc with lance and sword and longaxe with their ranks disorganized and having lost men and not merely horses to the arrows aimed at their flank the charge may not have even been delivered while borros and those who did reach the shieldwall would be caught between the enemy and the advancing stormlands foot without any room to reform or retreat making it easy for the riverlord infantry to kill the apparently unarmoured horses and dispatch their riders this is also an issue for the stormlands infantry that supposedly crashes into the riverlord shieldwall as these parties of cavalry could not be accommodated in their front ranks and would have to withdraw through openings between files in the formation assuming these existed the stormlands infantry would face the same challenges as their cavalry due to the poor ground lowlight conditions and enemy archery to which we can add the fatigue of advancing across the field with their arms and armour which would have a similarly disastrous effect on their formation while gyldan claims the shieldwall swayed and staggered back and seemed as if it might break when the stormlands infantry delivered their attack its doubtful that such a disorganized formation could have this effect adrian goldsworthy discussed this issue in the ancient greek context so ill quote him at length here it is very difficult even for welldrilled soldiers marching across a flat parade ground to move in a perfectly straight line for a distance of several hundred yards32 since each man takes his dressing from those on either side the entire unit will tend to conform to a shift in direction by one individual the spacings between each man may also fluctuate in most military parades you will see the soldiers halt to dress ranks at some point if a formation of welldrilled soldiers attempts to march across country then the problems of keeping position in the ranks and moving in a uniform direction are magnified enormously this is true on a dry flat plain still more on soft or boggy ground or any sort of slope no flat plain is perfectly flat least of all in greece there are always minor irregularities in the ground some battlefields were also broken by more substantial obstacles such as water courses or walls as a hoplite advanced the minor irregularities and unevenness of the ground would have caused him to veer to one side or other or slowed him down in comparison to the rest of the front rank these slight differences in direction or speed would have become more american politics in skorea we recently experienced a failed coup attempt by former president yoon sukyeol sometimes called the korean trump by critics what worries me is that i see structural and behavioral similarities between that case and patterns emerging in the us here is what happened in korea after losing the 2024 parliamentary elections president yoon effectively lost governing power and entered extreme confrontation with the legislature in response his camp promoted election fraud conspiracy theories attempted to escalate tensions with north korea and contributed to social instability on december 3 2024 yoon declared martial law police were used to block access to the national assembly and military units were deployed to prevent lawmakers from carrying out the constitutional vote to lift martial law this was a direct attempt to override democratic institutions using security forces the coup ultimately failed due to 1strong civilian resistance 2lawmakers insisting on constitutional procedures 3military units largely refusing to carry out aggressive or illegal orders now looking at the united states my concern is this if trumpaligned forces were to lose the 2026 midterm elections there is a nonzero risk that similar tactics could be attempted 1renewed claims of election fraud 2efforts to disrupt vote counting 3deliberate escalation of social unrest 4use of that unrest as justification for extreme measures such as invoking the insurrection act recent events make me uneasy 1national guard troops deployments in places like washington dcportland 2public threats to invoke the insurrection act in response to protests eg minnesota 3authoritarian rhetoric questioning the value of elections themselves i also worry that international events such as the military operation that removed maduros position in venezuelacould act as a psychological catalyst encouraging reckless or irrational decisions by leaders who feel cornered i sincerely hope this worst case scenario never happens but as someone who has lived through a real modern coup attempt in a democratic country i feel its important to raise the question if such a scenario were to unfold in the united states how should citizens institutions and state governments realistically respond to protect democratic processes im asking this in good faith and would appreciate thoughtful discussion
